edition.locus: Eusebius HE 5.1.11-14 (the ten who lapsed; daily arrests; the slaves' slander)

source_text: Ἐντεῦθεν δὴ διεκρίνοντο οἱ λοιποί, καὶ φανεροὶ καὶ ἕτοιμοι ἐγίνοντο πρωτομάρτυρες, οἳ καὶ μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας ἀνεπλήρουν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς μαρτυρίας, ἐφαίνοντο δὲ καὶ οἱ ἀνέτοιμοι καὶ ἀγύμναστοι καὶ ἔτι ἀσθενεῖς, ἀγῶνος μεγάλου φόβον ἐνεγκεῖν μὴ δυνάμενοι· ὧν καὶ ἐξέτρωσαν ὡς δέκα τὸν ἀριθμόν· οἳ καὶ μεγάλην λύπην καὶ πένθος ἀμέτρητον ἐνεποίησαν ἡμῖν καὶ τὴν προθυμίαν τῶν λοιπῶν τῶν μὴ συνειλημμένων ἐνέκοψαν· οἳ καίπερ πάντα τὰ δεινὰ πάσχοντες, ὅμως συμπαρῆσαν τοῖς μάρτυσιν καὶ οὐκ ἀπελείποντο αὐτῶν. Τότε δὲ οἱ πάντες μεγάλως ἐπτοήθημεν διὰ τὸ ἄδηλον τῆς ὁμολογίας, οὐ τὰς ἐπιφερομένας κολάσεις φοβούμενοι, ἀλλὰ τὸ τέλος ἀφορῶντες καὶ τὸ ἀποπεσεῖν τινα δειμαίνοντες. Συνελαμβάνοντο μέντοι καθ᾽ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν οἱ ἄξιοι τὸν ἐκείνων ἀναπληροῦντες ἀριθμόν, ὥστε συλλεγῆναι ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐκκλησιῶν πάντας τοὺς σπουδαίους καὶ δι᾽ ὧν μάλιστα συνεστήκει τὰ ἐνθάδε. Συνελαμβάνοντο δὲ καὶ ἐθνικοί τινες οἰκέται τῶν ἡμετέρων, ἐπεὶ δημοσίᾳ ἐκέλευσεν ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀναζητεῖσθαι πάντας ἡμᾶς· οἳ καὶ κατ᾽ ἐνέδραν τοῦ σατανᾶ, φοβηθέντες τὰς βασάνους ἃς τοὺς ἁγίους ἔβλεπον πάσχοντας, τῶν στρατιωτῶν ἐπὶ τοῦτο παρορμώντων αὐτούς, κατεψεύσαντο ἡμῶν Θυέστεια δεῖπνα καὶ Οἰδιποδείους μίξεις καὶ ὅσα μήτε λαλεῖν μήτε νοεῖν θέμις ἡμῖν, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ πιστεύειν.
pass_a_gloss: From this point then the rest were being separated, and first-rank martyrs became manifest and ready, who also with all eagerness were fulfilling the confession of the testimony, and there were also becoming visible the unready and untrained and still weak, not being able to bear the fear of a great contest; of whom also about ten in number fell away; who also produced great grief and immeasurable mourning for us and checked the eagerness of the rest who had not been seized; who although suffering all terrible things, nevertheless were present with the martyrs and were not leaving them. Then we all were greatly terrified on account of the uncertainty of the confession, not fearing the punishments being brought on, but looking to the end and dreading lest anyone fall away. Yet each day the worthy were being seized, filling up their number, so that there were collected from the two churches all the zealous and those through whom especially the affairs here stood together. And there were also being seized some pagan slaves of our people, since the governor ordered publicly that all of us be sought out; who also by a plot of Satan, having feared the tortures which they were seeing the saints suffering, with the soldiers urging them on to this, falsely accused us of Thyestean feasts and Oedipodean unions and things which it is not lawful for us either to speak or to think, but not even to believe.
pass_b_english: From this point onward the rest of us were sifted apart, and those who were manifest and prepared showed themselves as foremost martyrs, and with all eagerness they fulfilled the avowal of their witness; but there also appeared the unprepared and untrained and still weak, who could not bear the fear of a great contest, and about ten in number of them fell away. They caused us great sorrow and immeasurable grief, and they checked the eagerness of the rest who had not yet been seized, who, though suffering every terror, nevertheless stood beside the martyrs and did not abandon them. Then we were all greatly dismayed because the outcome of the confession was uncertain, for we did not fear the punishments being inflicted, but we looked to the end and dreaded lest anyone should fall away.

Yet day by day those who were worthy were seized to fill up their number, so that from the two churches all the earnest were gathered in, even those by whom especially our affairs here were held together. Some pagan household slaves of our people were also seized, since the governor had commanded publicly that all of us be hunted out, and these slaves, by a snare of Satan, feared the tortures which they saw the saints suffering, and, as the soldiers incited them to it, they falsely accused us of Thyestean banquets and Oedipodean unions and things which it is not lawful for us even to speak or to think, nor even to believe to be true.

choices.why: plural predicate nominative describing those distinguished as manifest and ready; context requires rank among confessors, not chronological first martyr
accusative object of ἀνεπλήρουν with genitive defining content; ὁμολογία is public confession and μαρτυρία is testimony under trial
adjectival accusatives preserving mythic reference to cannibalism and incest as stock slander; transliteration keeps the allusion visible
